topic: Canada Child Benefit: who receives it. CRA pays one person per household; when both parents live with the child, the female parent is usually considered primarily responsible (legislative requirement, Income Tax Act) and should apply; the male parent can apply with a signed letter from the female parent; same-sex parents: one parent applies for all children; the amount is the same whichever parent receives it

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): Maya and Dan live together with their 4-year-old; the July 2026–June 2027 maximum for a child under 6 is $8,157 a year (actual amount depends on adjusted family net income from the 2025 returns).

spoken.under6: eight thousand one hundred and fifty-seven dollars

sources.who: canada.ca CRA 'Who can apply – Canada child benefit': female parent living with the child usually considered primarily responsible; the other parent can apply with a signed letter from the female parent; same-sex parents: one parent applies for all children (via canada.ca search excerpts 2026-11-04)
sources.same: CRA Taxology podcast ep. 7 'Parenting perks' (canada.ca): presumption is a legislative requirement under the Income Tax Act; no matter which parent receives the CCB, the amount will be the same; CRA can only pay one person in the household
